lessons.title: Commercial Leases: Lock-Ins, Escalations and Who Pays What

children.text: In April 2020, with offices shut across India, landlords started receiving letters from tenants citing force majeure and asking for rent to be suspended. Two owners in the same Pune business park, with identical rents and similar tenants, had very different experiences. One lease clearly defined force majeure, capped any relief and kept the lock-in intact. The other was a downloaded template that said almost nothing. The first owner negotiated a short deferral. The second spent a year in arbitration. In commercial property, the rent is agreed in a meeting, but the income is really made in the lease document.

body.text: A commercial lease turns a building into a predictable income stream. Every clause, from lock-in to escalation to who pays maintenance, moves money between you and your tenant for years.

children.text: How a Commercial Lease Comes Together

markDefs.definition: A short, usually non-binding document summarising the key commercial terms of a lease, such as rent, deposit, lock-in, escalation and rent-free period, agreed before the full lease deed is drafted.

children.text: Commercial deals usually start with a
term sheet

or letter of intent listing the headline terms. Lawyers then draft the full lease deed. Because commercial leases run well beyond one year, the deed must be registered with stamp duty paid, and the parties negotiate who bears that cost. Tenants often pay it, but it is a negotiable point.

cells: 3 to 9 years for offices; longer for warehouses and built-to-suit

children.text: Lock-Ins: Your Income Insurance

The lock-in is what makes commercial income bankable. If a tenant leaves during the lock-in, a typical clause requires it to pay rent for the remaining lock-in months. Some leases also include a landlord lock-in, which stops the owner from ending the lease early.

body.caption: The exact wording varies by lease. Some leases let the deposit be adjusted against this amount.

body.text: A lock-in is only as strong as the tenant's ability to pay. If a struggling startup walks out owing 14 months of lock-in rent, you may have to go to arbitration or court to recover it. In practice, the security deposit is the protection you can actually use immediately.

children.text: Escalations: How Rent Grows

Indian office leases mostly use one of two escalation structures. A step-up of 15% every three years is the most common. Some leases, especially in retail and warehousing, use a fixed annual increase of around 5%. They sound similar, and 15% over three years equals about 4.77% a year compounded, but they produce different cash flows.

body.title: Monthly rent on a 9-year lease starting at ₹1,00,000

body.caption: Nine-year comparison on a starting rent of ₹1,00,000 a month

children.text: Step-up: Years 1 to 3 at ₹12 lakh a year = ₹36 lakh. Years 4 to 6 at ₹13.8 lakh = ₹41.4 lakh. Years 7 to 9 at ₹15.87 lakh = ₹47.61 lakh. Total: ₹1.25 crore.
Annual 5%: yearly rent of ₹12 lakh grows by 5% each year for 9 years. Total = ₹12 lakh × (1.05⁹ minus 1) ÷ 0.05 = ₹12 lakh × 11.03 = ₹1.32 crore.
Equivalent annual rate of the step-up: 1.15^(1/3) minus 1 = 4.77%. Even so, the step-up earns less in total, because rent stays flat for the first three years before each jump.
Who Pays What

markDefs.definition: A lease where the tenant pays base rent plus some or all of the property's running costs, such as common area maintenance and utilities, so the landlord's rent is closer to net income.

children.text: Most Indian office and retail leases work as a form of
net lease
: the tenant pays rent plus running costs of its own space, while the owner keeps a smaller list of ownership costs. The split is negotiable, so read it line by line.

body.caption: Typical cost responsibilities in an Indian office lease

cells: Paid to the building manager or association, per sq ft
Some leases pass increases on to the tenant
Tenant insures its own fit-out and contents
Warm shell usually commands higher rent
Return the space to its handover condition

body.label: What CAM covers
body.context: Security, cleaning, lifts, landscaping, common electricity and facility management for shared spaces. If a lease makes the landlord pay CAM, your net rent can fall by a meaningful amount every month.

children.text: Clauses That Quietly Shift the Balance

columns.label: Landlord-friendly
points: Escalation of 15% every 3 years or 5% a year
Narrow force majeure clause with a cap on relief
Tenant bears stamp duty, CAM and reinstatement

columns.label: Tenant-friendly
points: Small deposit or bank guarantee instead of cash
Broad force majeure allowing rent suspension

body.text: The force majeure clause matters more than most owners realise. After 2020, many tenants argued that lockdowns suspended their obligation to pay rent. Where leases defined force majeure narrowly and capped the relief, owners were far better protected. Never sign a lease that leaves this clause vague.

children.text: WALE: Measuring How Secure Your Income Is

markDefs.definition: Weighted Average Lease Expiry: the average remaining lease term across all tenants, weighted by the rent each pays. A higher WALE means income is locked in for longer.

children.text: Once you own more than one leased unit, or look at a REIT, you will meet
WALE
. It tells you, on average, how long the current rent is contracted to last.

Weighting by rent matters. A big tenant with one year left is a much larger risk than a small tenant with one year left, and WALE captures that. REITs such as Embassy Office Parks and Mindspace report WALE every quarter, and many also report the average time to lock-in expiry, which is often shorter and more realistic.

body.title: Calculate: WALE for a Two-Tenant Floor
body.prompt: You own a floor in a Gurugram building with two tenants. Tenant A pays ₹6 lakh a month with 6 years left on its lease. Tenant B pays ₹4 lakh a month with 1.5 years left. What is the WALE in years?
body.explanation: (₹6 lakh × 6 + ₹4 lakh × 1.5) ÷ (₹6 lakh + ₹4 lakh) = (36 + 6) ÷ 10 = 4.2 years. A simple average of the two terms would give 3.75 years, understating the security provided by the larger tenant.

body.title: Quick Check: Leaving During Lock-In
body.question: A tenant in Bengaluru pays ₹2.4 lakh a month under a lease with a 36-month lock-in. It leaves after 22 months. Under a standard lock-in clause, how much does it owe for the remaining lock-in?
body.explanation: Remaining lock-in: 36 minus 22 = 14 months. 14 × ₹2.4 lakh = ₹33.6 lakh. The ₹86.4 lakh option wrongly charges the full 36 months.

body.title: Scenario: Negotiating the Term Sheet
body.scenario: Meera owns a 5,000 sq ft office on OMR, Chennai. Market rent is about ₹70 per sq ft, or ₹3.5 lakh a month. A mid-sized IT firm wants a 9-year lease but asks for 6 months rent-free, a 12-month lock-in, escalation of 10% every 3 years, a 3-month deposit, and Meera to pay stamp duty.
body.prompt: What do these asks cost Meera, and how should she counter?
body.modelAnswer: Six rent-free months cost ₹3.5 lakh × 6 = ₹21 lakh, compared with ₹10.5 lakh for a more typical 3 months. A 10% escalation every 3 years instead of 15% cuts total 9-year rent from about ₹4.38 crore to about ₹4.17 crore, a loss of roughly ₹20.5 lakh. The 12-month lock-in is the bigger risk, because the tenant could leave after a year, often right after she has lost 6 months of rent to the rent-free period. A sensible counter: 3 to 4 rent-free months, a 36-month lock-in, 15% escalation every 3 years, a 6-month deposit, and stamp duty borne by the tenant or shared. She can trade: for example, accept 5 rent-free months if the tenant agrees to a 36-month lock-in and 15% escalation. A longer lock-in and a strong tenant also make the unit worth more if she sells it as a pre-leased asset.

cards.definition: A short summary of agreed lease terms, signed before the full lease deed is drafted.
The period during which the tenant must pay the remaining rent if it exits.
A scheduled rent increase, such as 15% every 3 years or 5% a year.
A lease where the tenant bears running costs such as CAM and utilities in addition to rent.
Common Area Maintenance: charges for security, cleaning, lifts and shared spaces.
Weighted Average Lease Expiry: average remaining lease term weighted by rent.
The tenant's obligation to return the space to its original condition at exit.

points: Commercial leases start with a term sheet and become registered lease deeds, with stamp duty responsibility open to negotiation.
Lock-ins make income bankable, but they are only as good as the tenant's ability to pay, so the deposit is your first line of defence.
15% every 3 years equals about 4.77% a year, yet earns less over 9 years than a steady 5% annual escalation.
Most Indian office leases work as net leases: tenants pay CAM and utilities, owners keep property tax and building insurance.
Force majeure, sub-letting and reinstatement clauses quietly shift risk and must be read carefully.
WALE, weighted by rent, shows how long your income is contracted; the time to lock-in expiry is often the more realistic figure.

body.text: Market practices, rents and lease terms described in this lesson are indicative and vary by city, asset and negotiation. Lease deeds are legal documents; have them reviewed by a qualified lawyer. This lesson is educational and is not legal advice or a recommendation to buy or lease any property.
